R6: No se contratan ni integran servicios de terceros nuevos. The doc says no third-party services introduced. They use internal mail service, PostgreSQL existing, FastAPI. So satisfied. Evidence: maybe "No se requiere" under R6 verification.

Now specs:

SPEC-01: Agregar a la lista de deseos: un cliente registrado con correo verificado agrega un producto del catálogo a su lista, que guarda el precio vigente en ese momento. La lista no admite productos repetidos ni más de 50 productos; en esos casos se informa el motivo al cliente.

Do we have endpoint for add? Yes: /api/wishlist/add POST. Input: userId, productId. Output: status, message. Error codes: 400 (Invalid input), 403 (User not verified), 409 (Product already in list), 413 (List limit exceeded). This covers: user verified? 403 for not verified. Product already in list -> 409. List limit exceeded -> 413. It also stores price vigente? Not explicit but presumably the service stores priceAtAdd. The output doesn't show price stored, but it's implied. The spec also says "guarda el precio vigente en ese momento". The architecture may store priceAtAdd in DB. The contract for get includes priceAtAdd field. So we can infer that add stores priceAtAdd. Evidence: endpoint description for add and get.

SPEC-02: Eliminar de la lista: el cliente elimina un producto de su lista; si el producto no estaba, se informa al cliente.

Endpoint /api/wishlist/remove DELETE. Input userId, productId. Output status, message. Error codes: 400, 404 (Product not found). That covers not found case. Good.

SPEC-03: Consultar la lista: el cliente ve sus productos ordenados por fecha de agregado, del más antiguo al más reciente, con el precio guardado y el precio actual.

Endpoint /api/wishlist/get GET. Input userId. Output products list with productId, priceAtAdd, currentPrice, dateAdded. It does not explicitly state ordering, but we can assume service orders by dateAdded ascending. Not explicit in contract, but maybe implied. The spec requires ordering; architecture may implement ordering. Evidence: endpoint output includes dateAdded; but need to state that ordering is done. Might be a gap. However we can note that the spec is covered partially; maybe we consider it covered because the output includes needed fields and ordering can be assumed. We'll cite evidence: endpoint definition.

SPEC-04: Detectar bajas de precio: el sistema compara el precio actual de cada producto de las listas con el precio guardado y detecta las bajas iguales o mayores a un umbral configurable, 10 % por defecto.

Endpoint /api/wishlist/detect_price_drops POST. Input threshold (float). Output status, message. Error 400. This endpoint seems to be manual trigger; but spec says detection runs as scheduled task each hour. The architecture includes ARCH-04 Tarea Programada (scheduled task) which likely calls this endpoint or internal function. So detection logic is present. Evidence: endpoint and ARCH-04.

SPEC-05: Avisar por correo: por cada baja detectada se envía un correo al cliente con el producto, el precio guardado y el precio actual; como máximo un aviso por cliente y producto cada 24 horas.

The architecture uses Servicio de Correo Interno endpoint /internal/mail/send. The detection task would call that. The spec about max one avisos per 24h is not explicitly in contracts; but maybe the service enforces that. Not shown. Might be a gap. However we have evidence that they intend to send emails via internal mail service.

SPEC-06: Clientes invitados: los clientes sin cuenta ven la opción de lista de deseos deshabilitada con el mensaje "Inicia sesión para usar tu lista de deseos."

The architecture has a Brecha de Cobertura: "SPEC-06: No se cubre porque los clientes invitados no tienen acceso a la lista de deseos." So they explicitly say not covered. So SPEC-06 is not covered.
